 Gift (Act) Received 2026/05/22 
 Nature
 - Handmade fan earrings
- Handmade ribbon skirt
- Tall white leather mukluks
- Embroidered mittens
The value of this gift is over $1000
 Source
 David Monias, Chief of Pimicikamak Cree Nation
 Circumstances
 This handmade gift was presented to me during my visit to Cross Lake while attending meetings in the community. It reflects the richness of Indigenous art, history, and culture, and shows the exceptional skill and craftsmanship of Indigenous artisans. 
In recognition of the gift’s cultural significance and symbolic meaning, the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner has determined, in accordance with subsection 11(3) of the Conflict of Interest Act, that it is not to be forfeited to His Majesty in right of Canada. I am therefore able to proudly wear it as a representation of the talent, heritage, and traditions of Indigenous communities. 
 The records for all 26 declared gifts are available in the Declarations and Other Documents section below. 
 Travel
 Travel aboard a private aircraft.
Date: July 10, 2026
Accepted from: the Government of Québec
Circumstances: Travel between Sept-Iles and Montreal after the commercial option was delayed. This flight was required as part of my official duties as Minister of Indigenous Services.
 Recusal
 In the exercise of my official duties as Minister of Indigenous Services, I recused myself on May 26th, 2026, from a discussion or decision regarding the re-appointment of Robert Kanatewat to the Cree-Naskapi Commission in order to avoid any conflict of interest between my official functions and the private interest of Robert Kanatewat with whom I hold a pre-existing relationship.
